description.short: Adventure Parc Snowdonia at Dolgarrog is a multi-activity adventure hub in the Conwy Valley, at the gateway to Eryri National Park. Reopened in 2025 under new ownership, it offers indoor climbing, high ropes, underground caving, ninja assault courses, zip lines, gorge walking, camping pods, and on-site dining — all framed by mountain scenery.

description.full:
Adventure Parc Snowdonia occupies a dramatic site in the Conwy Valley, backed by the Carneddau mountains and surrounded by the landscapes of Eryri (Snowdonia) National Park. The site has a striking history: it opened in August 2015 as Surf Snowdonia, the world's first commercial artificial surfing lake — a 300m x 110m freshwater lagoon producing consistent shoulder-high waves — and attracted extraordinary early interest, with 14,000 visitors in its first two weeks and 97% occupancy in its debut season. The venue rebranded as Adventure Parc Snowdonia in 2019 to reflect a wider programme of land and aerial activities. Following the closure of the wave lagoon in September 2023 due to mechanical failures, the site passed through a brief period under Zip World before being acquired by the Interesting Hotels Group, who reopened it in September 2025.

The current offer centres on a large indoor adventure zone — Adrenaline Indoors — alongside outdoor activities and accommodation. Indoor activities include a ninja assault course with 9m and 12m freefall towers, an adventure climbing wall with ten routes, a high ropes course, a 100-metre underground caving maze, and freefall/drop experiences. Outside, guests can take on a zip line, a pump track and skate bowl, pickleball courts, gorge walking, cycling, and hiking. Camping pods sleep four and the on-site Caffi Eryri restaurant serves locally sourced food Wednesday to Sunday. The Interesting Hotels Group also operates the Ixora Hotel and Spa nearby. The venue holds Adventuremark accreditation and a Council for Learning Outside the Classroom (LOtC) Quality Badge, making it suitable for school and youth groups.

The surf lagoon remains on site but is not currently in operation under the current ownership.
